en: Sanjaya said: Arjuna was overcome with pity, his eyes full of tears and troubled. Krishna spoke to him in his sorrow.
Krishna said: Arjuna, where has this weakness come from at such a hard moment? It does not suit a noble person, it does not lead to heaven, and it brings dishonour.

first: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते ।
en: Son of Pritha, do not give in to cowardice; it is not worthy of you. Throw off this small weakness of heart and stand up, you who burn your enemies.

first: कथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन ।
en: Arjuna said: Madhusudana, how can I shoot arrows in battle at Bhishma and Drona? They deserve my respect, destroyer of foes.

first: गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान् श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके ।
en: It is better to live in this world even by begging than to kill these great and honoured teachers. If I kill them, even the wealth and pleasures I enjoy here will be stained with blood.

first: न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः ।
en: We do not know which is better for us: that we win, or that they win. The sons of Dhritarashtra stand before us, and if we kill them we would not even want to live.
My nature is weighed down by pity, and I am confused about what is right. I ask you: tell me for certain what is best for me. I am your student; I come to you for help. Teach me.
I see nothing that could remove this grief which dries up my senses, even if I won an unrivalled, rich kingdom on earth or even rule over the gods.
Sanjaya said: Having said this to Krishna, Arjuna told Govinda, "I will not fight," and fell silent.
O Bharata, then Krishna, as if smiling, spoke to the grieving Arjuna there between the two armies.
Krishna said: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words that sound wise. The wise do not grieve for the dead or for the living.

first: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः ।
en: There was never a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these kings. And none of us will ever stop existing in the future.
Just as the soul in this body passes through childhood, youth and old age, it passes on to another body. A steady person is not confused by this.
Son of Kunti, the contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These come and go and do not last. Bear them patiently, Bharata.

first: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ ।
en: The steady person who is not shaken by these, who stays the same in pain and pleasure, is fit for immortality.

first: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः ।
en: What is unreal does not come into being, and what is real never stops being. Those who see the truth know the final nature of both.

first: अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।
en: Know that what fills this whole world cannot be destroyed. No one can destroy what does not change.
These bodies of the eternal, indestructible and immeasurable soul are said to have an end. So fight, Bharata.

first: य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम् ।
en: One who thinks the soul kills, and one who thinks it is killed, both do not understand. It does not kill, and it is not killed.

first: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः ।
en: The soul is never born and never dies. It did not come into being, and it will not stop being. It is unborn, eternal, lasting and ancient. It is not killed when the body is killed.
Arjuna, how can a person who knows the soul to be indestructible, eternal, unborn and unchanging kill anyone or cause anyone to be killed?

first: वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि ।
en: Just as a person throws away worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the soul leaves worn-out bodies and enters new ones.

first: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः ।
en: Weapons do not cut it, fire does not burn it, water does not wet it, and wind does not dry it.
It cannot be cut, burned, wetted or dried. It is eternal, present everywhere, firm, unmoving and ancient.
It is said to be unseen, beyond thought and unchanging. So, knowing it like this, you should not grieve.

first: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् ।
en: And even if you think it is always being born and always dying, mighty-armed one, you still should not grieve for it.

first: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च ।
en: For one who is born, death is certain, and for one who dies, birth is certain. So you should not grieve over what cannot be avoided.
Beings are unseen at the beginning, seen in the middle, and unseen again at the end, Bharata. What is there to grieve about in this?
One person sees the soul as a wonder, another speaks of it as a wonder, another hears of it as a wonder. Yet even after hearing, no one truly knows it.
The soul living in every body can never be killed, Bharata. So you should not grieve for any creature.
Looking at your own duty as well, you should not waver. For a warrior there is nothing better than a fight for what is right.
Arjuna, happy are the warriors who get such a battle, coming by itself like an open gate to heaven.

first: अथ चेत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि ।
en: But if you do not fight this rightful battle, you will give up your duty and your good name, and you will earn sin.
People will speak of your disgrace for ever. And for an honoured man, disgrace is worse than death.
The great chariot-fighters will think you ran from battle out of fear. Those who once thought highly of you will think little of you.
Your enemies will say many unkind things and mock your strength. What could be more painful than that?

first: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम् ।
en: If you are killed, you will reach heaven; if you win, you will enjoy the earth. So stand up, son of Kunti, determined to fight.
Treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same, and then get ready to fight. In this way you will not earn sin.

first: एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां शृणु ।
en: I have told you this understanding as taught in Sankhya. Now hear it as taught in Yoga. Joined with this understanding, you will break the bonds of action.
On this path no effort is wasted and there is no harm in it. Even a little of this practice saves one from great fear.
Here the determined mind is single and steady, Arjuna. The minds of those who are not determined are scattered in endless directions.
Unwise people who delight in the words of the Vedas speak flowery words and say, "There is nothing else."
Full of desires and aiming at heaven, they describe many rituals that bring rebirth as the fruit of action and lead to pleasure and power.
Those attached to pleasure and power, their minds carried away by such words, do not gain a steady, determined mind fixed in meditation.
The Vedas deal with the three qualities. Arjuna, rise above the three qualities and the pairs of opposites. Stay always in goodness, free from the wish to gain and keep, and be centred in the self.
As much use as there is in a small well when water floods everywhere, that much use there is in all the Vedas for a wise person who knows Brahman.
Your right is to the work alone, never to its results. Do not let the result be your reason for acting, and do not be attached to not acting.

first: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनंजय ।
en: Arjuna, do your work steady in yoga, giving up attachment, and staying the same in success and failure. This sameness of mind is called yoga.
Action done for results is far lower than action done with a steady mind, Arjuna. Take shelter in this understanding. Those who act for results are pitiable.
One whose mind is steady leaves behind both good and bad deeds even in this life. So devote yourself to yoga. Yoga is skill in action.

first: कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः ।
en: The wise, with steady minds, give up the results born of action. Freed from the bond of birth, they reach the state beyond sorrow.
When your mind crosses the swamp of delusion, you will lose interest in what you have heard and what is still to be heard.
When your mind, confused by many teachings, stands firm and unmoving in deep meditation, then you will reach yoga.
Arjuna said: Keshava, how do you describe a person whose wisdom is steady and who is fixed in meditation? How does such a person speak, sit and walk?
Krishna said: Son of Pritha, when a person gives up all the desires of the mind and is content in the self, by the self, that person is said to have steady wisdom.
One whose mind is not troubled in sorrow, who does not long for pleasure, and who is free from attachment, fear and anger, is called a sage of steady wisdom.
One who is not attached to anything, who neither rejoices nor hates on meeting good or bad, has steady wisdom.
When a person draws the senses back from their objects on every side, as a tortoise draws in its limbs, that person's wisdom is steady.
When a person does not feed the senses, their objects fall away, but the taste for them remains. Even this taste goes away when one sees the Supreme.
Son of Kunti, the restless senses forcibly carry away the mind even of a wise person who is trying hard.

first: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः ।
en: Having controlled them all, one should sit steady, intent on me. One whose senses are under control has steady wisdom.
When a person thinks about the objects of the senses, attachment to them grows. From attachment comes desire, and from desire comes anger.
From anger comes confusion; from confusion, loss of memory; from loss of memory, the ruin of understanding; and when understanding is ruined, the person is lost.
But one who moves among the objects of the senses with the senses under control, free from liking and disliking, and master of oneself, reaches peace.
In that peace all sorrows end. The mind of one who is at peace soon becomes steady.
One who is not steady has no clear understanding and no deep feeling. Without such feeling there is no peace, and without peace, how can there be happiness?
When the mind follows the wandering senses, it carries away one's understanding, just as the wind carries a boat off course on the water.
So, mighty-armed one, the person whose senses are fully held back from their objects has steady wisdom.

first: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी ।
en: What is night for all beings, the self-controlled person is awake to. What all beings are awake to is night for the sage who sees.
Just as waters enter the ocean, which is always being filled yet stays still and unmoved, so the person into whom all desires enter in this way finds peace, not the one who chases desires.
The person who gives up all desires and lives free from longing, without the sense of "mine" and without ego, finds peace.

first: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति ।
en: Son of Pritha, this is the state of Brahman. Reaching it, one is no longer confused. Staying in it even at the hour of death, one reaches the peace of Brahman.
